newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey court rejects Erbakan compensation case.
newsitem.headline: Turkey court rejects Erbakan compensation case.

text.p: A Turkish criminal court on Thursday refused to hear a compensation case opened by former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan against a top prosecutor who is attemping to ban Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party.
"Ankara criminal court rejected a compensation case opened by Welfare and its leader Necmettin Erbakan against appeal court chief prosecutor Vural Savas," Anatolian news agency said.
It said the criminal court ruled that the case must be handled by a higher court.

Erbakan has demanded 20 billion Turkish lira ($132,000) from Savas for allegedly insulting him and Welfare at a news conference in May in which he announced he was seeking the party's closure by the constitutional court in an anti-Islamist crackdown.
Erbakan left office last week under intense pressure from the strictly secularist military after a stormy year as modern Turkey's first Islamist leader. ($1 = 151,220)
